- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate mean price when sentiment is neutral or mixed; use 20-day moving average as baseline for correction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.67 range with no clear direction, model often fails to capture volatility; add ±1.5% buffer around forecast for next 7 days.
